attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, made without quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: 'Guaranteed' is firm, so this is scorable. The normalised wording drops 'any' and 'virgin' (new), but the generic 'will face' keeps the universal scope and the no-backstop condition. No deadline is stated.

contract.note: Reading the rates as all-in borrowing costs and requiring cash-flow evidence for 'near-impossible' is an ordinary plain reading. The meaning of 'backstopped' and the cost basis are the evaluator's choices, so the result depends on interpretation.

evidence.note: Nebius company disclosure: a corporate 364-day facility at SOFR+2.75-3.50% with mixed uses. It is not shown to be a project financing without a backstop, and the all-in cost is not given, so it is not a counterexample.
Digi Power X release about a conditional SPV commitment with no interest rate and no closing. It cannot test the 9-14% range.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm, open-ended forecast. The packet has no completed qualifying financing with verified all-in terms and no project cash-flow evidence. The Nebius corporate facility does not meet the early-resolution rule, so nothing in the packet settles the claim either way.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion and his own estimate, in his own post.

semantics.note: Both share thresholds are kept, and the 80% figure is kept as his estimate. The 'illusion of demand' part is a causal gloss on top of the concentration figures.

contract.note: Treating the shares as supplier revenue attributable to the two labs, measured market-wide, is a reasonable reading of the context. However, the denominator, the period (Q2 2026) and what counts as 'compute sales' are all the evaluator's choices.

evidence.note: Bloomberg estimate that OpenAI made up about 70% of Microsoft's AI revenue in the fiscal year to June 2026. It covers one supplier and an annual period, so it cannot settle the market-wide shares.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no market-wide denominator for AI revenue or for compute sales. The only figure covers a single supplier (Microsoft) over a different period, so neither threshold can be confirmed or refuted.

attribution.note: This is Zitron's own rebuttal to a position he describes, so the assertion is his and is endorsed.

semantics.note: Revision 2 matches the sentence faithfully: no rival comes near on growth or customer base, and the labs' customers are mostly AI startups.

contract.note: Treating 'customers' as paying customers and the latest quarter as the period are reasonable choices. 'Mostly' measured by count rather than revenue is a contestable choice the speaker did not make, so the result depends on interpretation.

evidence.note: Ramp sample showing business adoption and spending concentration. It does not classify customers as AI startups and is not market-wide.
Google company disclosure: Gemini passed 1B monthly users. These are free and consumer users, not paying customers, and there is no matched growth comparison with the labs.

reviews.rationale: Nothing in the packet classifies the labs' customers as startups or not, and there are no comparable paying-customer counts or matched revenue growth figures. The Gemini user figure does not meet the contract's paying-customer measure, so the claim stays unsettled.

attribution.note: Zitron's own estimate. He cites his own earlier piece, which is still his claim.

semantics.note: The 'would have' counterfactual (repricing the same bonds at current rates) is preserved, along with the over-$7B threshold and the two stated causes.

contract.note: The method (lifetime undiscounted interest over the original tenor, at publication-date rates) is a fair plain reading. But the contract marks interpretation as not decisive, and I disagree: across roughly 311B principal-years, using original versus remaining tenor and new-issue versus secondary yields could move the total either side of $7B.

evidence.note: Oracle's September 2025 prospectus gives the six tranches, coupons and maturities. These are inputs only; it has no October 6 repricing.

reviews.rationale: The original bond terms are confirmed, but there are no admissible October 6, 2026 yields for all six tranches. Without them the counterfactual calculation cannot be checked against the $7B threshold.
